report:
Summary finding
- The difference is primarily a change in the model’s residual at the first token (position 0) across many middle-to-late layers — i.e., a changed prior / bias for the start-of-sequence token.  
- The logit-lens top tokens for the high-norm cells are dominated by tokens that commonly appear as sentence/document starters or headline-style capitalized words (examples across layers: "Stay", "Every", "Do", "Best", "Coming/Coming", "Major", "Later", "Author", plus topic words like "law", "tragic", "surgeon", "clinic", "Royals", "bottle", "wings"). That pattern is consistent with a shift in what the model prefers to emit at the very beginning of text generation.
- The evidence does not support naming a single semantic objective or domain (the favored tokens are heterogeneous: some are generic sentence-starters, some are news/headline/tragedy-related, some are object tokens). So the safest interpretation is a positional/prior shift rather than a clear, specific behavioral objective.

Key evidence and reasoning
- Norms: the L2 norm is overwhelmingly concentrated at pos0 across nearly all layers (very large numbers for p0 in layers ~4–25), with much smaller norms at later positions. That indicates the difference signal is injected or active at sequence-start and propagates through many layers.
- Logit-lens: the high-norm cells at pos0 point toward capitalized/initial tokens and headline-like words in later layers (and some lower-layer cells point to concrete nouns like "bottle"/"wings"). This is consistent with changing the distribution of first tokens the model will produce (or expect) rather than changing a fine-grained attribute that appears later in generation.
- No coherent single theme: tokens span multiple topical clusters (generic sentence starts, commerce/objects, and tragedy/legal/clinic words). That heterogeneity means there’s no clear, specific semantic objective evidenced (e.g., "more legal wording" or "more tragedy content") that I can confidently name.

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not available here (or not shown), which would help confirm how the positional bias affects full continuations. Without that, I rely mainly on positional norms + logit-lens tokens.
- It’s possible the difference encodes a mixture of small biases that only become interpretable in context; the data here best supports the positional/prior-shift interpretation.

Conclusion
- Characterisation supported by the evidence: Model B differs from A mainly by introducing a strong change to the residual stream at the first token (position-0) that shifts the model’s prior over initial tokens toward certain capitalized/headline-like and sentence-start tokens.
- The evidence does not support naming a more specific semantic objective or domain.
